public_rationale: On April 14, 2025, OpenAI released GPT-4.1 at $2 per million input tokens and $8 per million output tokens, reporting prices 26% below GPT-4o for median queries [e1]. This release preceded the April 28 cutoff and contradicts the claim that newer models only become more expensive [e1]. OpenAI's February 27 announcement described GPT-4.5 as more expensive than GPT-4o, but that comparison does not establish a consistently rising price trend [e2; e1].
limitations: These disclosures concern customer API prices, not OpenAI's internal inference spending or cost per completed task.
The 26% comparison uses OpenAI's median query mix and does not establish savings for every workload.

our_interpretation: The adjacent per-token figures identify customer API prices as the ordinary measure of expensive.

criteria.support_condition: Published API prices show that successive comparable recent OpenAI models consistently became more expensive.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Before the post, OpenAI released a comparable newer model at lower API prices than its predecessor or the existing model it was replacing.
